comparator.name: International and European Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026/27 curriculum defines a common 60-EC first year followed by a choice between the International and European Law and Technology Law tracks. Because the normalized target is generic, the broad International and European Law track is selected under the least-specialized/general rule rather than for UCR fit. It contains 60 EC in each year, a compulsory 30-EC exchange semester, and a 10-EC bachelor-concluding Research Colloquium in which students design and defend an independent research paper. The pathway totals exactly 180 EC.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces eleven history, politics, sociology, sustainability and communication courses with programming, data science, networks, databases, machine learning, AI ethics, digital strategy, business-and-AI analysis and applied market research. The two programmes share 13 courses and differ by 11 courses (82.5 EC) each way, comfortably clearing the 30-EC floor.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target has two formal tracks. The International and European Law track is the broadly representative, less specialized route focused on the programme's named international and European legal identity; Technology Law is a narrower specialization and is retained as evidence for a distinct UCR direction rather than substituted into the comparator.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Law, Society & Justice is completed in semester 1 before every advanced UCR law course. Introductory politics, business and sociology precede advanced EU politics, international relations, social theory and regulation. All formal prerequisites occur earlier, all courses are offered in their assigned Fall 2026 cohort term, and eight 300-level courses are included.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad international, European, constitutional, human-rights, cross-border, business-law, governance and legal-politics interests. The formal Technology Law track and the technology-law/digital-regulation interests support a genuinely different second programme, implemented through law plus data, computing, AI ethics and digital-business governance. After that inclusion, all generator-eligible interests are owned; no third coherent direction remains, so production stops at two.

notes.text: UCR offers a substantial interdisciplinary law sequence in international, EU, constitutional, human-rights, criminal, private and transnational business law. It does not reproduce Groningen's complete specialist sequence in administrative regulation, judicial protection, legal English, commercial dispute resolution, competition law, exchange and required legal research.
